title: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Amritsar
summary: Sri Harmandir Sahib, also called the Golden Temple, stands in the middle of the Amrit Sarovar in Amritsar and is described as the central religious place of the Sikhs. Its foundation was laid in December 1588 under Guru Arjan, who installed the Guru Granth Sahib in it in 1604. He had it built on a lower level than its surroundings and open on four sides.

uncertainty.note: Start is the foundation date (December 1588, SGPC; 1645 Bikrami Samvat). The SGPC page also says the building work was completed in 1601 CE in the same sentence that gives August/September 1604 (Bhadon Sudi 1st, 1661 Bikrami Samvat) as the installation of the Guru Granth Sahib; 1601 is not used. End is the present: the shrine stands, after being demolished and rebuilt in the 18th century per the SGPC.

importance.justification: The Amritsar district administration calls it the central religious place of the Sikhs; India placed it on its UNESCO Tentative List in 2004.

reviewer_note: Sacred site; described neutrally. No model written: the pages opened give a 67 ft square platform, a 40.5 ft square temple and the first-floor roof at 26 ft 9 in (SGPC), but no total height, so the height-plus-plan rule is not met. The UNESCO Tentative List point (31°38' N, 74°53' E) is only to the minute and lies about 1.5 km from the OSM point, so the OSM point is used. Least sure of: the 1601 versus 1604 completion wording on the SGPC page.
